page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz with AWS Neoverse-N1 cores. The instance allocates dedicated CPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, eliminating hyperthreading. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and features a cache configuration of 64 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU hardware included, meaning all storage relies on network-attached EBS volumes.

The instance is optimized for network and EBS performance, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48563.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11689.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 973.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.38. Memory bandwidth performance is mixed, showing high throughput for small cached blocks at 1894.04 GB/sec, but dropping to 181.11 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, resulting in a weak overall Passmark memory score of 1817.53.

Given its hardware profile, the c6gn.8xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that benefit from high network throughput and dedicated ARM cores without requiring high memory-to-CPU ratios. It demonstrates solid performance in multi-threaded tasks, such as software compilation with a Geekbench clang score of 25637.0, static web serving at 33.08 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations at 38.79 million operations per second. However, it is less suited for single-threaded tasks or memory-intensive operations. Appropriate workloads include high-performance web serving, network appliances, multi-threaded batch processing, and distributed database operations.
